title: Urgent lane answer
description: Designed (docs/native/capture-split.md 4.3 "The route", #773), not implemented. The hub's answer to `POST /api/station/urgent`. 200: `ok`, `gen` and one result per item it took; an item missing from `results`, or answered with a word the sender does not know, was not taken: it is tried again at most 5 times, after the healthy items and in a request of its own, and then counts as `rejected`. 400 `bad_json`, 413 `too_large`, 422 `bad_batch`: `error` and `reason`; the request was refused whole and nothing of it was applied; the sender cuts it to single items, and an item refused alone is `rejected`, finally. 401, 403, 409: `error` and `reason` as on every station route (station-error.schema.json): kept and retried every 30 s. 503 with a Retry-After header: the hub is not the leader and NOTHING was applied; its body is today's, `error` and `updating`. Only a 200 that names an item `applied`, `duplicate` or `stale` makes it sent.

gen.description: On a 200: the hub's fencing generation, a count (lease.schema.json `counter`: an integer up to 2^53 - 1, or a string of decimal digits). Compared by value (5 and "5" are one), for change only. When it is another than the last one seen, the sender sends again every alarm answered under another generation at or after its last sighting of the old one minus 120 s. The answer to `GET /api/station/hello` carries it too (capture-hello-answer.schema.json).

results.description: On a 200: one entry per item taken, in any order.

error.description: On a 4xx or 5xx: a sentence for people. Fixed text, never the token.

reason.description: On a 4xx: why, as one word a program can act on. The route's own are `bad_json`, `bad_batch` and `too_large`; a refused token gets station-error.schema.json's words.

updating.description: On a 503: the hub is deploying or this task is not the leader.

result.title: One item's answer
result.description: What the hub did with one item of the request, named by its (key, rev).

status.description: `applied`: taken and acted on (an alarm raised or joined to the open alarm it belongs to, a page's live state set). `duplicate`: this (station, key) is already there as raised or stale (an alarm), or this rev is the one held (a page); nothing new was raised. `stale`: taken, too old to act on (an alarm at or past the hub's age limit: a late notice, no push; a page rev below the one held). `rejected`: the hub will never take this item. The first three mean sent.
